name: prose-1k-1
input:
Here are some notes I have been collecting, just for background mood and vocabulary.

| Recipes and `recipe new` | **partial** | 7 recipes in `recipes/` (Qwen2, Qwen3, Qwen3.5 dense / MoE / VL, Llama, Gemma 4), so "Qwen3 family only" no longer holds; unsupported architectures refused at load |
| Plan compiler, `plan show`, measured-memory KV, graph capture | **partial** | graphs are captured per batch row count for batched decode (`crates/intarsia-core/src/model/graph_step.rs`); no tuning DB, no `--allow-slow` |
| Scheduler | **partial** | FIFO continuous batching (`crates/intarsia-core/src/scheduler.rs`) on Metal, CUDA and HIP (dense models on Metal and HIP since #154, hybrid models on all three); tensor-parallel batching and MTP under batching are not on main; no priorities |
| Watchdog and supervisor | **implemented** | `crates/intarsia-server/src/supervisor.rs` |
| Paged KV blocks | **planned** | KV is contiguous per slot |
| Radix-tree prefix cache | **partial** | opt-in content-addressed prefix store (`crates/intarsia-core/src/prefix_store.rs`, `serve --prefix-store`, hash-keyed pages, not a radix tree), single-sequence engine only; idle-slot prefix reuse with recurrent snapshots otherwise |
| Host-RAM KV tier | **partial** | the prefix store keeps prefix pages in host memory and on disk (`crates/intarsia-core/src/prefix_store.rs`); live per-slot KV has no host tier |
| Speculation | **partial** | n-gram (Metal only) and the MTP drafter (`--spec mtp` on CUDA, HIP and Metal, one sequence, greedy; captured draft+verify step on HIP in `crates/intarsia-core/src/model/spec_graph.rs`); DFlash2 block drafter opt-in on HIP (`--spec dflash`, Qwen3.8-27B, tp=1 and tp=2; #175, cost lane dcp: `docs/results/2026-10-27-dcp-dflash-cost.md`; `crates/intarsia-core/src/model/dflash2.rs`); batched MTP refused at load (`crates/intarsia-models/src/load.rs`) |
| Sampler and structured output | **partial** | no min-p or penalties; `llguidance` is in |
| Tool and reasoning parsers | **partial** | one tool-call format (hermes) and one reasoning format (think-tags) |
| Tensor parallelism and `Comm` | **partial** | NCCL (CUDA), 2-rank P2P (HIP), host-bounced for the rest; no RCCL, no fused all-reduce+norm+quant, no lossy transports; batching under tp, vocab-parallel head and fused all-reduce+norm are open PRs, not on main |
| Accuracy system | **partial** | `intarsia accuracy` and `qualify`; gates differ from section 6 (see ADR-0008) |
| Bench plugins, onboarding | **partial** | `bench speed` and `onboard` exist; no `BenchPlugin` trait, no `micro` plugin |
| OpenAI and Anthropic APIs | **partial** | `/v1/responses` and `/v1/embeddings` absent |
| Prometheus metrics | **implemented** | OTLP export absent |
| Containers, run manifest, `intarsia replay` | **partial** | script-level only: `scripts/deploy.sh`, `scripts/bench-bundle.sh` (pack / replay), `scripts/repro-build.sh`, CI `scripts/repro-check.sh`; only HIP dev Dockerfiles (`deploy/tatooine/`); no `intarsia replay` command, and the bundle holds no plan or tuning hash |

---

## 0. Goals, honest targets, anti-goals

Requirements in priority order (user, 2026-10-12): modular → easy to use → accurate → fast (top 3 per platform) → reproducible → OpenAI/Anthropic APIs → built-in UI/TUI (optional, dark) → metrics → live architecture diagram → Spark → R9700 → TP=X → Intel Arc later.

**What "top 3" means per platform** (the competitor to beat at each phase gate):

| Platform | Current leaders on our boxes | Phase-2 gate | Phase-4 gate |
|---|---|---|---|

name: prose-1k-2
input:
Here are some notes I have been collecting, just for background mood and vocabulary.

ing | required | Tensor prefix of the MoE block, e.g. `"model.language_model.layers.{i}.mlp"`; the loader finds router, experts and shared expert under it. Expert counts and widths come from `config.json`. |

### `[layer.gemma]` (Gemma 4 decoder layer, one block per layer)

| Key | Type | Default | What it controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | required | `"gemma4"` (the only layout implemented). |
| `prefix` | string | required | Tensor prefix of the whole layer, e.g. `"model.language_model.layers.{i}"`. Everything under it (attention, dense MLP, router, experts, the five norms, `layer_scalar`) is found by the fixed Gemma 4 names. Head sizes, KV heads, sliding window, rope tables, soft-cap and expert counts come from `config.json` (`ModelDims::gemma`, `layer_types`). Use `pattern = ["gemma"]` and `[layer.norms] pre_gemma = <input_layernorm>`. |

### `[layer.dsv41_attn]`, `[layer.dsv41_moe]` (DeepSeek-V4.1, `recipes/deepseek_v41.toml`)

Name the checkpoint layout of the DeepSeek-V4.1 graph (`intarsia_core::dsv41`, contract in docs/design/dsv41-ops.md):
`prefix` (the attention / MoE tensors), `hc` (the hyper-connection mix weights of the sub-block), `norm` (its pre-norm)
and, on the attention, `engram` (the Engram projection on `engram_layer_ids`). The graph itself is code and reads
`config.json` directly; family `deepseek_v41` refuses to load for generation until the executing lanes land, and
`intarsia plan show --model <dir>` lists its op sequence from the safetensors headers alone.

### `[top]` (required)

| Key | Type | Default | What it controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `embed` | string | required | Token embedding tensor. |
| `final_norm` | string | required | Final norm tensor. |
| `lm_head.tensor` | string | required | Output projection tensor. |
| `lm_head.tied_to` | string | none | Tensor to reuse when `lm_head.tensor` is absent from the checkpoint (or `tie_word_embeddings` is set). A missing head without this is a load error. |

### `[defaults]`

| Key | Type | Default | What it controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kv_dtype` | string | `"bf16"` | KV cache dtype: `bf16`, `f16`, `f32` or `fp8_e4m3`. Override per run with `--kv-dtype`. Anything but `bf16` changes numerics ([tuning.md](tuning.md)). |
| `max_batch` | int | `1` | Most sequences a run may decode together. `--max-batch N` above it is refused; without the flag the value is clamped to what the engine implements (continuous batching is Metal only, up to 8). |
| `fp8_act` | string | `"static"` | FP8 checkpoints: `"static"` quantises activations with the checkpoint's `input_scale` (W8A8), `"none"` keeps them 16-bit (W8A16). No effect on other formats. See [quant-moe.md](quant-moe.md). Override with `--fp8-act`. |
| `w4a4_as_w4a16` | bool | `false` | A checkpoint that declares plain `NVFP4` (weights AND 4-bit activations, W4A4) is refused by the loader (`Gemma4` layers) and not covered by the recipe in `recipe new` / `onboard`, because the engine runs NVFP4 weight-only (W4A16): a deviation from the declared scheme and from vLLM. `true` accepts that knowingly (Gemma-4 NVFP4 does). |

Here are some notes I have been collecting, just for background mood and vocabulary.

* A bug is far outside: attention output x1.05 failed 7/6 aggregate checks and 10 of 10 prompts in both modes; x1.01 failed
  mean KL, tail-bucket KL and top-5 in prefill, mean KL in decode, and 3 + 1 prompts with the envelope (3 + 3 with fixed
  margins only: on this dense model the envelope removes none of them); `matmul:1.0` (every output one ulp off, 14x the
  rel_l2 of the envelope's perturbation) failed 9 + 7 prompts and the aggregates; x1.002 is not distinguishable from a
  correct build (the same prompt `code` that a correct build failed). 2x the envelope's rel_l2 (`matmul:2e-2`) failed one
  prompt per mode and the prefill aggregate top-1: the resolution of the gate is about a factor of 2 in rel_l2.

So: treat k = 2 as a pre-registered default, not as a calibrated false-positive rate. A prompt that fails with `k needed`
below about 3 is inside the spread of correct builds; one with `k needed` above 5 is not. For a hard per-prompt verdict
record at least 4 perturbations or raise `--envelope-k`; with one or two (all the 35B window could afford) read the
`k needed` column next to the verdict.

### Which code produced a baseline (provenance)

Review finding 1: the "before" baseline used to be recorded from the new tree with kernels switched off, and nothing
said which code made it. Switching off kernels cannot switch off the device-position rope / kv_append / attention
kernels, the split-KV grid or the loader changes, and a typo in `INTARSIA_CUDA_DISABLE` silently left the new kernel on.
Now:

* A build stamps itself. `INTARSIA_BUILD_STAMP` (the output of `scripts/tree-stamp.sh`: `head=<sha> code-tree=<hash>
  dirty=yes|no`, plus `overlay=<paths>`) is passed to `cargo build` and read with `option_env!`. The build boxes get the
  tree without `.git`, so the binary cannot ask git itself; `scripts/phase1b-acceptance.sh` computes the stamp on the Mac.
  A binary built without it is "unstamped" and its baselines and self-goldens are refused.
* A baseline and a self-golden store that stamp. The gate (`--pre-change SHA`, `--revlist FILE`) accepts a baseline only if
  its head is the declared pre-change commit or an ancestor of the code under test (`git rev-list HEAD` of that tree,
  written where the history is), the two code trees differ (a self-comparison proves nothing: `--allow-same-code` for
  reproducibility checks), and the baseline's tree is clean. The one allowed exception is the **harness overlay**: the
  pre-change engine has no baseline or self-golden support, so "before" is a build of the pre-change commit plus only the files
  in `HARNESS_OVERLAY_PATHS` (`accuracy.rs` and its three submodules, which read engine output and never change it). Its
  stamp says `dirty=yes overlay=...` and the gate accepts exactly that. The build under test must be clean (`--allow-dirty`
  for development).
* Kernel disable list: a baseline recorded with `INTARSIA_CUDA_DISABLE` / `INTARSIA_HIP_DISABLE` set is refused (it is not
  the pre-change code). The variables themselves now reject names that match no registered kernel when the device opens.
* Printed, never refused: `--no-graphs`, the resolved kernel per op, differences from the recorded run. If nothing differs
  the run says so ("a kernel or graph change cannot show up in this comparison").

### Same-weights regression gate: `--write-self-golden` / `--self-golden`
